subject: Realtime pipeline congestion and intermittent websocket stalls - customer escalation
messages:
From: Samir Gupta <samir@neurofin.ai>
To: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 13 Aug 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: [PROD] Live chat: repeated token stream stalls and elevated 5xx rate

Dylan —

We started seeing intermittent stalls in our live chat yesterday evening around 19:40 UTC. The client sees streaming tokens for a few seconds, then the stream pauses for ~10–30s before resuming; sometimes the stream drops with a 502/504 and the client reconnects. Overall response latency is up ~3–5x and our 5xx rate has climbed from ~0.2% to ~4.8% during peak traffic. Throughput (requests/min) is also below expected on several nodes.

Impact: this affects a handful of real-time billing customers; user-facing product quality is degraded.

Attached: neurofin-debug-log-20270813.txt (contains request/response IDs and local traces), screenshot-ws-trace.png

Can you confirm this is on Redwood's side and any immediate mitigation we can do? This is urgent for our SRE and account team.

—Samir
Ops, NeuroFin

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai, Samir Gupta <samir@neurofin.ai>
Cc: rachel_kim@redwood.ai, dev_patel@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 13 Aug 2027 18:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: [PROD] Live chat: repeated token stream stalls and elevated 5xx rate

Investigation update (prelim):

What we've seen so far:
- Edge proxies are returning intermittent 502/504 around the same timestamps Samir included. The proxy logs show TCP connection resets that align with websocket keepalive gaps.
- Inference hosts show backpressure events where token-emit loops block for bursts followed by a catch-up (token bursts then gaps). No OOMs.
- Correlation: most stalled connections are tied to sessions that use long context windows ( > 8k tokens) and heavy streaming keepalive churn.

Immediate mitigations we can try (low-risk):
1) Route affected sessions to a fallback model variant with smaller KV working set (reduces kernel tail latency).
2) Tighten the proxy's websocket idle timeout and explicit ping frequency to avoid long-lived half-open connections; this reduces silent TCP stalls.
3) Enable temporary request-level preforking on the busiest inference pool to spread long-context requests across more worker processes.

I've attached a trimmed debug log with the interesting timestamps. Att: neurofin-debug-log-20270813.txt (text/plain, ~2.3MB).

Will continue debugging kernel-level traces; will post an update within 90 minutes.

—Marissa
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference
From: Samir Gupta <samir@neurofin.ai>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 13 Aug 2027 20:10:12 -0700
Subject: Re: [PROD] Live chat: repeated token stream stalls and elevated 5xx rate

Thanks Marissa — appreciate the quick look.

A few clarifications from our side:
- The affected sessions are production customers using long-system prompts (≈9k tokens) combined with streaming for UI responsiveness.
- We tried increasing client-side reconnect backoffs but that only reduces symptom frequency; the user experience is still unacceptable.
- This is impacting a top-10 revenue account; our account team is requesting a call with Redwood leadership if this cannot be temporarily mitigated within the hour.

Can you confirm whether routing to a smaller-KV model variant can be done without a full rollback? If so please do it and let me know the expected cutover time.

—Samir
From: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, samir@neurofin.ai
Cc: rachel_kim@redwood.ai, dev_patel@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 14 Aug 2027 08:00:00 -0700
Subject: RE: [PROD] Live chat: repeated token stream stalls and elevated 5xx rate

Executive summary for leadership (quick read):
- Symptom: intermittent websocket-streaming pauses (10–30s) and spike in 5xx errors; correlated with long-context streaming sessions (~8–10k tokens).
- Scope: NeuroFin production traffic (subset of regions); measurable spike in 5xx (to ~4.8%) and ~30% drop in sustained throughput on affected clusters.
- Immediate mitigations proposed (approved for immediate rollout if leadership OKs):
  * Route long-context streaming sessions to a smaller-KV model variant (no code rollback; config-level routing). Expected cutover: 4–7 minutes to update routing rules, 15–30 minutes for traffic to stabilize.
  * Increase proxy ping frequency and reduce idle timeout to avoid silent TCP stalls (requires config push to edge fleet; 2–5 minutes rolling deployment).
  * Temporarily enable a conservative per-request concurrency cap on the busiest inference pool to reduce burst-induced backpressure.
- Tradeoffs: slightly higher per-token latency for requests moved to the smaller model variant; customer-visible latency should improve overall due to reduced stalls.
- Ask: Rishi — approve routing & proxy config change and sign off on offering a one-time service credit to NeuroFin if they request it.

If approved I will coordinate the runbook and notify Samir.

—Dylan
Senior Customer Reliability Manager, Redwood Inference
